Uncapped or excluded exposures: travel up to 10% of services fees (about $245,000 on $2.45M of services), change orders at a blended $210/hr with no rate card, and optional finite scheduling and sandbox add-ons outside the total.

Change orders priced at a single blended $210/hr with no role-based rate card.

pricing.oneTimeCosts: Fixed-fee implementation services of $2,270,000 (Year 1 $1,450,000; Year 2 $820,000) plus training and change management of $180,000 (Year 1 $120,000; Year 2 $60,000). Integration platform and EDI partner is priced as a recurring line ($95,000 in Year 1, $60,000 per year after) and is treated as recurring pending clarification.
pricing.recurringCosts: Subscription totals $3,737,300 over 5 years, rising from $690,000 in Year 1 to $807,200 in Year 5 at a 4% cap. Integration platform and EDI partner totals $335,000. Premium support is $0. Optional finite scheduling ($54,000 per year) and additional sandbox ($18,000 per year) are excluded from the total.
pricing.totalCostSummary: 5-year total on the pricing sheet is $6,522,300, covering subscription for 650 users, fixed-fee implementation, integration platform and EDI partner, and training and change management. Response p.7 states a $6.84M TCO that does not match the sheet and must be reconciled; travel, change orders and optional modules sit outside this total.

totalCost.gaps: Response p.7 states a 5-year TCO of $6.84M, which is $317,700 above the pricing sheet total and must be reconciled. Outside-the-total exposures: travel up to 10% of services fees, change orders at a $210/hr blended rate with no role rate card, optional finite scheduling at $54,000 per year and additional sandbox at $18,000 per year. Implementation is shown by year, not by phase as RFP section 5 requires. Riverbend internal effort is not estimated. Exit data export is free only within 90 days of termination.
totalCost.rationale: Pricing sheet is complete at summary level and arithmetically consistent. 5-year total of $6,522,300 comprises subscription $3,737,300, fixed-fee implementation $2,270,000, integration platform and EDI $335,000, and training and change management $180,000 (Summary tab). Subscription escalator is capped at 4% per year with renewal terms for years 6-7 (Assumptions tab; p.7). This gives a predictable core cost.

strategicFit.gaps: No vendor viability evidence such as financials, ownership, customer base or retention. No target operating model or growth discussion for multi-entity or multi-plant expansion. Flexibility to add entities or modules is not described beyond optional add-ons.
strategicFit.rationale: Quarterly releases with a sandbox preview show an upgrade cadence (p.4). Renewal at the same terms for years 6-7 supports continuity (Assumptions tab). The AI-assisted demand planning roadmap item (GA planned 2027) is explicitly out of scope and is not credited (p.7).

technicalFit.gaps: No migration tooling, validation, reconciliation or balance-cutover approach. No performance or scalability evidence for about 650 users across 4 plants and 2 DCs. Integration platform is described as included (p.4) but priced as a separate line of $335,000 over 5 years (Summary tab). Administration model is not described.
technicalFit.rationale: Architecture is credible: multi-tenant SaaS on a US-only region, REST and event APIs, prebuilt Salesforce and ADP connectors, and MES at Plant 2 via the integration platform (p.4). Data migration is described only as Phase 1 data migration of GL history and masters (p.5). No approach is given for 7 years of GL, open transactions or about 42,000 SKUs. BAI2 banking and the EDI VAN are not addressed (p.4 against scope on p.3).

functionalFit.gaps: No demonstrated scenarios or fit-gap detail for the 3 legal entities, CAD/MXN, fixed assets, cash management or consolidation beyond the table. Finite scheduling is an optional add-on (p.3; Optional tab, $54,000 per year) and is not in the 5-year total. Configurator effort falls within Riverbend's schedule. EDI depends on a partner.
functionalFit.rationale: Functional coverage table (p.3) rates multi-entity GL with native multi-currency and automated intercompany eliminations, procure-to-pay with three-way match and contract pricing, lot/serial and RF scanning, MRP and shop floor, and quality/CAPA as Standard. Configure-to-order is rated Configuration (rules-based configurator, 6-8 weeks to model product lines, p.3). EDI is delivered through a certified partner (p.3). Specific standard-coverage claims are credible evidence for a 3.

experienceTeam.gaps: Reference contact details are not in the response despite references provided on p.5; not yet verified. Named team beyond the lead and availability commitments are not provided. Delivery is through Northline's in-house professional services with no subcontractors stated.
experienceTeam.rationale: Named lead Priya Raman has 14 years of experience and has led 6 cloud ERP go-lives in industrial manufacturing (p.5), well above the two required. Three industrial components references at 250-900 users, each live within 12-15 months, report average close time reduced from 9 to 4.5 days (p.6). Reference scale is comparable to Riverbend's about 650 users.

supportService.gaps: Resolution targets, response times for lower priorities and escalation path are not defined. Premium support is priced at $0 on the Summary tab, so whether 24x7 coverage is included in subscription is unclear. Account management beyond the named CSM is not described.
supportService.rationale: 24x7 Priority 1 support with a 1-hour response SLA and a named customer success manager (p.7). Quarterly releases with a 4-week sandbox preview (p.4) support ongoing maintenance. Training and super-user network are part of change management (p.5).

usabilityAdoption.gaps: No demonstration evidence for finance, procurement, shop-floor or order-to-cash user journeys. No accessibility statement. Training hours and adoption effort for about 650 users are not quantified. Mobile app claims are unverified.
usabilityAdoption.rationale: Response offers role-based training, a super-user network and stakeholder analysis within change management (p.5), and a mobile scanning app that works offline (p.3). No demonstrated workflows, screens, navigation or role-specific experiences are shown. Accessibility is not addressed. Evidence is thin for a 3.

securityCompliance.gaps: Reports and the ISO certificate are not attached; verification is pending. Data protection detail (encryption at rest and in transit, key management, retention, privacy obligations) is not described. Exception handling and penetration testing are not addressed.
securityCompliance.rationale: SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II reports are issued annually, latest June 2026, and ISO 27001 is certified (p.4). Controls include SSO via SAML/OIDC, role-based access with a segregation-of-duties rule library, and a full audit trail (p.4). US-only hosting supports the residency requirement (p.4). Evidence is specific and credible for a 3.

implementationApproach.gaps: Staffing mix by role is not shown beyond the lead. No risk register or mitigation plan. Item master cleansing before month 3 is a Riverbend dependency with limited lead time. Cutover detail and go-no-go criteria are thin. Overlap of phases in months 6-8 needs a resource plan. Riverbend's 8 SMEs at 50% are not costed.
implementationApproach.rationale: Phase plan is specific: Phase 1 in months 1-8 (finance, procurement, GL history migration) and Phase 2 in months 6-13 (inventory, warehouse, manufacturing, EDI). Each phase has design, build, three test cycles (SIT, UAT, parallel close) and a cutover rehearsal (p.5). Approach is fixed-fee and phase-gated (p.2). Staffing is 11 consultants at peak, 80% onshore (p.5). Dates fall inside Riverbend's targets (p.2 against RFP section 3).

result.overview: Northline offers a largely standard-coverage cloud ERP with a specific, fixed-fee, phase-gated plan that lands finance and procurement at 8 months and manufacturing and warehouse at 13 months, inside Riverbend's 9- and 14-month targets, led by a named lead with six comparable go-lives. All five mandatory requirements appear met on the face of the response, though the SOC reports, ISO certificate and references are claims not yet verified. The main concerns are commercial: the response states a 5-year TCO of $6.84M while the pricing sheet totals $6,522,300, and travel, change orders and optional modules sit outside that total. Data migration detail, banking and EDI VAN approach, and demonstrated scenarios are thin and should be clarified before the committee finalizes scores.

Named implementation lead with 6 cloud ERP go-lives in industrial manufacturing, and three comparable industrial references at 250-900 users, with reported close time reduction from 9 to 4.5 days (p.5-6).
Fixed-fee, phase-gated plan with finance and procurement at 8 months and manufacturing and warehouse at 13 months, inside Riverbend's 9- and 14-month targets (p.2, p.5).
Core functional coverage rated Standard across multi-entity GL, procure-to-pay, inventory, MRP and quality (p.3).
Subscription escalator capped at 4% per year with renewal terms for years 6-7 stated, supporting predictable core cost (Assumptions tab).
clarificationQuestions: Reconcile the $6.84M 5-year TCO on response p.7 with the $6,522,300 pricing sheet total and confirm which figure is binding.
Confirm whether the integration platform is included in subscription (p.4 says included) or charged separately ($335,000 over 5 years), and what it covers.
Provide implementation fees by phase, a role-based rate card for change orders, and a cap or estimate for travel.
Confirm whether 24x7 Priority 1 support is included in subscription given the $0 premium support line, and provide resolution targets and escalation path.
Describe the data migration approach for 7 years of GL history, open transactions and about 42,000 SKUs, and how BAI2 banking and the EDI VAN will be integrated.
Provide the current SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO 27001 certificate, and describe encryption, key management and data retention controls.
Provide scripted demonstrations of finance close, configure-to-order for pump assemblies, and lot/serial inventory; confirm whether finite scheduling is required and its cost.
Provide reference contacts for the three industrial references and the lead's go-lives, plus vendor financial viability evidence and exit terms beyond the 90-day export window.

Core functions depend on roadmap, customization or third-party add-ons: supplier portal (2027), serial tracking, configurator (400 hours), shop-floor data collection; integrations not addressed.

totalCost.rationale: 5-year total of $4,094,400 is stated and reconciles across years and line items (pricing sheet, Pricing tab). Subscription escalator of 7% annually after Year 2 is applied consistently (sheet: $480,000 to $513,600 to $549,600 to $588,000). strategicFit.gaps: No evidence of vendor viability, product direction, upgrade path, or customer base; roadmap dependency for a core procurement function.
strategicFit.rationale: Supplier portal is on a 2027 roadmap (response p.3), which is not credited as current capability. SOC 1 audit is in progress (p.4). Claims of a scalable global delivery model are stated without specifics (p.2). No vendor viability, financial, or customer-base information is provided.

technicalFit.gaps: Integrations entirely unaddressed; migration approach and tooling absent; no architecture, performance, or admin information; EDI VAN and MES connectivity unpriced.
technicalFit.rationale: Hosting on a major public cloud in US regions is stated (response p.4). Data migration is placed on the client: client extracts and cleanses data into vendor templates, and the partner loads (p.5). No approach is given for 7 years of GL history, about 42,000 SKUs, or open transactions. No integration approach for Salesforce, ADP, Plant 2 MES, BAI2 banking, or EDI VAN (p.3 scope vs response). No architecture, scalability, performance, or administration detail.

functionalFit.rationale: Multi-entity, multi-currency GL with consolidation is stated as standard (response p.3). Supplier portal is a 2027 roadmap item and is not credited (p.3). Serial tracking is via customization (p.3). Shop-floor data collection relies on a third-party add-on that the client licenses separately (p.3; pricing Notes). Pump configurator needs about 400 hours of custom development (p.3; pricing sheet Configurator line, $72,000). EDI is quoted separately on request (pricing Notes). No demonstrations or scenario responses for procurement, quality holds, or order-to-cash are provided.

experienceTeam.gaps: No named lead; no go-live references; delivery partner and subcontractor responsibilities not identified; no evidence of comparable scope or complexity (multi-entity, manufacturing, EDI).
experienceTeam.rationale: The response contains no comparable ERP projects, reference customers, or team qualifications (response pp.1-6). The implementation lead is to be named at contract signature (p.5). The delivery partner is not named (p.2, p.5). The team mix is 3 onshore and 9 offshore (p.5), but no evidence of experience is provided. This is a substantial gap against the requirement for comparable experience.

supportService.gaps: No SLAs, escalation procedure, support coverage hours, or account management; no release and upgrade cadence; no post-go-live training detail beyond train-the-trainer.
supportService.rationale: Annual support fees are priced at $48,000 in Year 1 rising to $58,800 in Year 5 (pricing sheet, Support line). No service levels, support hours, escalation path, account management, or release/maintenance commitments are described in the response.

usabilityAdoption.gaps: No usability evidence. Request scenario demonstrations for finance close, procurement, warehouse and shop-floor users, an accessibility statement, and an adoption and training plan for about 650 users.
usabilityAdoption.rationale: Not evaluated. The response contains no demonstrated workflows, navigation examples, accessibility information, or role-specific user experience. The only related content is a train-the-trainer training approach (response p.5).

securityCompliance.gaps: No SOC 1 Type II; no detail on data protection, offshore access controls, or privacy; no bridge controls offered during the gap period.
securityCompliance.rationale: SOC 2 Type II report is available (response p.4). Role-based security and audit logging are stated (p.4). SOC 1 Type II is in progress and expected Q3 2027 (p.4), so the mandatory SOC 1 requirement is not currently met. No detail on encryption, access reviews, or incident response. Offshore delivery team of 9 (p.5) raises data-access questions that are not addressed.

implementationApproach.gaps: Big-bang timing conflicts with finance-first phasing and 9-month finance/procurement target; one SIT cycle is thin for 4 plants and 2 DCs; no cutover, change management, or client-resourcing plan for 8 SMEs at 50%; implementation lead unnamed.
implementationApproach.rationale: Proposes a single go-live in month 10 for all modules (response p.2, p.5). Client requires finance and procurement live within 9 months and a phased rollout starting with finance (RFP p.4). Staffing is 3 onshore and 9 offshore consultants (p.5). Testing is one SIT cycle plus UAT (p.5). Training is train-the-trainer only (p.5). No cutover plan, change management approach, risk register, or client-dependency plan. Implementation is agile in name only.

result.overview: Cypress Ridge offers a clear, fully itemized 5-year price of $4.09M and a US-hosted, SOC 2 Type II platform with multi-entity, multi-currency GL. However, it fails two mandatory requirements: the SOC 1 Type II report is not available until Q3 2027, and no implementation lead is named. Functional gaps (supplier portal on the 2027 roadmap, custom configurator and serial tracking, shop-floor add-on, unaddressed integrations) and a single big-bang go-live at month 10 add material delivery risk. Cost is understated because implementation is uncapped T&M and several items are excluded.

assumptions: Subscription escalator of 3% annually; sheet figures reconcile to this.

pricing.oneTimeCosts: Implementation fixed fees of $1,810,000 (Phase 1 $980,000 in Year 1; Phase 2 $310,000 in Year 1 and $520,000 in Year 2) plus change management of $230,000 (Years 1 and 2), for $2,040,000 total. pricing.totalCostSummary: Five-year total of $5,577,100 (about $5.58M): subscription $2,973,100, implementation $1,810,000, change management $230,000, managed services $384,000 and EDI managed service $180,000. totalCost.gaps: Client contingency of $129,000 equals 10% of $1.29M, not of total fixed implementation fees of $1.81M, which would be $181,000. Optional 24x7 uplift of $42,000 per year and change orders at $195 per hour are excluded from the total. No renewal or exit terms. totalCost.rationale: Pricing sheet is arithmetically consistent: the 5-year total of $5,577,100 matches the $5.58M stated on response p.7, the year totals reconcile, and the 3% subscription escalator is applied correctly. Implementation is fixed fee by phase. Material gaps remain: data migration is unpriced, connector costs are unlisted, the contingency is miscalculated, and several variable and optional costs sit outside the total. Value relative to scope cannot be benchmarked from the documents.

strategicFit.gaps: No roadmap, growth plan or target operating model discussion. No vendor viability information for H&V or Meridian. Because the platform is licensed through the integrator, continuity of licensing and direct Meridian commitments are unclear. Any future-release items should be treated as roadmap, not current capability.
strategicFit.rationale: Twice-yearly releases with automated regression testing (response p.4) support ongoing upgrades. H&V describes itself as a manufacturing-focused integrator with 22 manufacturing implementations (p.2, p.6), which indicates relevant domain depth.

technicalFit.gaps: No data migration approach, tooling or portability terms for 7 years of GL history, open transactions and ~42,000 SKUs. Plant 2 MES connector is recommended but not confirmed. BAI2 banking and EDI VAN integration approach not addressed. No performance or scalability evidence for ~650 users across 4 plants and 2 distribution centers.
technicalFit.rationale: Stated: Meridian hosted in US data centers (p.4), Meridian Integration Cloud with prebuilt Salesforce and ADP connectors (p.4), EDI through H&V managed service (p.4), and twice-yearly releases with automated regression testing (p.4). Architecture, scalability, performance and administration are not described.

functionalFit.gaps: Unaddressed scope areas listed above. No demonstration or workflow walkthrough evidence. The Plant 2 MES connector is recommended but not confirmed as an existing product or as configuration rather than custom work. EDI with 14 distributors is covered only by the managed service line, not by functional detail.
functionalFit.rationale: Headline claims are specific and mostly standard: native multi-entity GL with 3 entities and 3 currencies (response p.3), full procure-to-pay with supplier portal (p.3), lot and serial tracking, RF scanning and cycle counting (p.3), MRP and routings (p.3), and 4 pump and valve configurators already built on Meridian with an accelerator (p.3). The configurator experience directly fits Riverbend's pump-assembly configure-to-order scope. However, several in-scope areas are not addressed: quality holds and non-conformance, shop-floor data collection, three-way match, fixed assets, cash management and consolidation depth. No scenario demonstrations were provided.

experienceTeam.gaps: Reference letters are cited as attached but are not in the documents reviewed, so outcomes are unverified. No team bios or qualifications provided beyond the lead. Subcontractor roles (EDI managed service and any third-party resources) are not described.
experienceTeam.rationale: 22 Meridian implementations for manufacturers with $150M to $1B revenue (response p.6). Two comparable references: a valve manufacturer with 5 plants live in 13 months and a pump OEM with 3 plants live in 11 months (p.6). Named lead Chris Dunleavy has 4 Meridian go-lives in industrial manufacturing (p.5). The profile closely matches Riverbend's pump and valve, multi-plant mid-market context, which exceeds the minimum requirement.

supportService.gaps: No P2 to P4 response times, escalation path, service credits or account management model. 12x5 coverage for four plants with production systems may leave off-hours plant issues unsupported unless the 24x7 option is purchased. Post-go-live training approach is not described.
supportService.rationale: Post-go-live managed services at 12x5 with a 2-hour P1 response (response p.7). 24x7 coverage is available only as a paid option at $42,000 per year (Options & Rates tab). Managed services fee is $96,000 per year from Year 2. Release support is covered by twice-yearly releases (p.4).

usabilityAdoption.gaps: No demonstrated workflows, screenshots, navigation or role-specific experience shown. Accessibility is not addressed. Training hours and volumes are not quantified. No adoption results from prior Meridian projects are provided.
usabilityAdoption.rationale: Adopt-First methodology starts with day-in-the-life prototypes per role in month 2 (response p.5). Role-based training is included, with a dedicated 2-FTE change workstream and 4 weeks of floor support after each go-live (p.5). These are specific adoption plan elements that address training and adoption effort.

securityCompliance.gaps: Access controls, role-based security, encryption, audit logging, privacy commitments, incident response and breach notification are not described. The reports are not attached to the response. Confirm they cover the hosted service and whether H&V or Meridian operates it, and request any exceptions noted.
securityCompliance.rationale: SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II reports issued annually (response p.4) and US data center hosting (p.4) are named certifications and a stated hosting location. This meets the core requirement with credible evidence, and the related mandatory items pass.

implementationApproach.gaps: Data migration approach is missing, although the RFP requires it. No detailed phase plan, milestones, risk register or responsibility matrix. Riverbend's 8 internal SMEs at 50% allocation are not reflected in the vendor's dependencies. Phase 2 at month 14 leaves no schedule buffer against the RFP's 14-month limit.
implementationApproach.rationale: Two-phase plan with Phase 1 finance and procurement live in month 9 and Phase 2 operations live in month 14 (p.2, p.5), matching Riverbend's target dates. Testing includes SIT, two UAT cycles, a parallel month-end close and two cutover rehearsals per phase (p.5). Team is 10 consultants at peak, 100% onshore (p.5). Change management is a dedicated workstream (p.5).

result.overview: Harbor & Vine Digital proposes Meridian Cloud ERP licensed through H&V, with a two-phase rollout that matches Riverbend's 9-month finance/procurement and 14-month operations targets. All five mandatory requirements pass on stated evidence, subject to verifying the SOC reports and reference letters, which were cited but not included in the documents reviewed. The response is strongest on comparable manufacturing experience and a structured testing and adoption approach. Material gaps remain in data migration, pricing completeness, coverage of several in-scope manufacturing functions, support coverage, and vendor and licensing structure.

strengths: Strong comparable experience: 22 Meridian manufacturing implementations, plus a pump OEM (3 plants, live in month 11) and a valve manufacturer (5 plants, live in month 13) as references (response p.6).
Timeline matches the RFP: Phase 1 finance and procurement live in month 9 and Phase 2 operations in month 14 (response p.2, p.5).
Relevant prior work: 4 pump and valve configurators already built, directly relevant to Riverbend's configure-to-order scope (response p.3).
Structured testing and adoption: day-in-the-life prototypes by month 2, two UAT cycles, a parallel month-end close, two cutover rehearsals per phase and 4 weeks of floor support (response p.5).
Security baseline stated: SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II reports issued annually, with US data center hosting (response p.4).
clarificationQuestions: Provide the SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II reports for the hosting entity, confirm whether H&V or Meridian operates hosting, and disclose any exceptions.
Describe the data migration approach for 7 years of GL, open transactions, ~42,000 SKUs, customers and suppliers, and price it as a separate line item.
Confirm which integrations are prebuilt versus custom (Salesforce, ADP, Plant 2 MES, BAI2, EDI VAN) and price each connector.
Provide scenario demonstrations or walkthroughs for quality holds and non-conformance, shop-floor data collection, three-way match, fixed assets and cash management.
Correct the contingency to 10% of total fixed implementation fees and confirm whether it is included in the 5-year total.
Provide an assumptions tab, escalators for managed services, EDI and change-order rates, and P2 to P4 service levels with an escalation path.
Explain the contracting and licensing structure for Meridian through H&V, and provide renewal pricing after Year 5 along with data export and exit terms.
Separate Meridian's current capabilities from roadmap items, and provide vendor viability information and the reference letters for the two cited customers.

theme.summary: Evaluators see Northline Cloud ERP as functionally strong, particularly in finance, close and consolidation, and warehouse mobility, with a credible implementation approach. The main reservations center on cost: it is the highest-priced option, with an escalator that compounds, and pricing documentation that appears internally inconsistent. Some capabilities, such as finite scheduling and configurator setup, carry additional effort or cost.

theme.summary: Evaluators see Cypress Ridge Systems as the lowest-priced option, but its headline cost is considered unreliable. Multiple reviewers flagged that it does not meet the mandatory SOC 1 Type II requirement until 2027, which matters for external audit. Concerns also center on implementation risk, including a big-bang go-live approach and an unnamed implementation lead.

theme.summary: The committee sees Harbor & Vine Digital as a credible, well-structured delivery partner with a strong change-management approach and fixed-fee pricing at a mid-range level. Evaluators value its post-go-live floor support and reusable accelerators. Two gaps recur: the data migration approach is not adequately described, and support coverage or licensing terms raise dependency and cost questions.
